title: Material Passport Tool-Artifact Provenance Entry
description: One entry in Material Passport Schema 9 tool_artifact_provenance[] aggregate (Tool Paper route, v3.4.0). Scholar-entered at Stage 1 intake — NOT writer-emitted. Records the intake + disclosure layer for a NON-BIBLIOGRAPHIC artifact the scholar built or holds and brought back as primary evidence for a Tool Paper (Design & Evaluation). Named tool_artifact_provenance (NOT artifact_provenance) to stay lexically distinct from the pre-existing artifact_provenance FIELD in preregistration_artifact.schema.json and cross_document_source_manifest.schema.json, which describes something else. ARS does not build artifacts, does not auto-fill provenance, and does not judge whether the artifact is well designed, useful, clinically safe, or validated (route non-goals, carried verbatim into the integrity gate Phase C5 wording). The entry backs manuscript claims that cite it via claim_intent_manifest.planned_artifact_ids[]. Cross-array invariants AP-INV-1..AP-INV-4 are designed for lint enforcement in scripts/check_claim_audit_consistency.py (upstream; the script is not present in every checkout — JSON Schema cannot express cross-array integrity). See academic-paper/docs/tool-paper-route.md for the route design, worked example, and model-tiering statement.

artifact_id.description: Scholar-chosen identifier, flat within ONE Material Passport (a passport is one run). AP-INV-1 enforces in-passport uniqueness. FROZEN at Stage 1 intake: once tool_artifact_intake_declaration.status == artifacts_declared is set, this is the stable key space writers reference via planned_artifact_ids. A post-intake rename is a re-intake event (re-run the manifest emitters), NOT a silent edit — AP-INV-2 FAILs a passport whose planned_artifact_ids dangle after a rename.

title.description: Human-readable label for the artifact (e.g., 'NINM Safety parameter explorer v1.0.1 — safety-thresholds.js').

artifact_kind.description: What kind of non-bibliographic artifact this is. simulation_scenario/simulation_output stay distinct from usability_data/pilot logs so the integrity gate's simulated-framing rule (Phase C5 check 5) can key on them; process_artifact covers intermediate development artifacts (task inventories, concept lists, value-set counts — the development-process-paper pattern).

locator.description: Where the artifact physically lives. ARS reads nothing from the locator automatically — it is disclosure, not a fetch instruction.

path_or_uri.description: Local path or URI of the artifact (e.g., 'src/js/safety-thresholds.js' or a repository URL).

version_or_commit.description: Version tag or commit hash the declared content_units were measured on.

sha256.description: Optional content hash pinning the exact artifact bytes.

produced_by.description: Who produced the artifact. 'third_party' artifacts still need the scholar to declare their content_units; third-party provenance is a disclosure fact, not a trust grade.

description.description: Optional free-form description of what the artifact is and how it was produced.

content_units.description: Per-result-unit record of what this artifact contains that a manuscript claim can rest on. minItems 1 — an artifact entry with no content unit is a degenerate declaration that backs no claim (mirrors experiment planned_vs_executed minItems 1). artifact_alignment_result.unit_pointer points INTO this array (artifact_id alone is too coarse for a claim like 'mean screening time 92 s').

unit_id.description: Unit identifier unique within this artifact entry (e.g., 'pilot-time-crossover').

description.description: What this unit is (e.g., 'per-participant screening time in the pilot crossover').

quantity.description: Optional count/quantity the unit reports (e.g., 12 walkthrough issues, 40 concepts).

value.description: Optional reported value for the metric (number or string).

result_file.description: Pointer to the scholar's result artifact backing this unit (path/URI).

negative_findings.description: Declared null/absent/contradicting findings about the artifact or its evaluation. The KEY MUST be present (Phase C5 check-0 absent-key rule, ported from #260 D6 check-0); an empty [] is well-formed and routes to the check-4 advisory. An ABSENT key is malformed → gate FAIL. A manuscript claim that contradicts a negative_findings entry is NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_PROVENANCE, not merely a disclosure advisory.

known_limitations.description: Declared material limitations of the artifact/evaluation. The KEY MUST be present (Phase C5 check-0); empty [] is well-formed and routes to the check-4 advisory; an ABSENT key is malformed → gate FAIL. Surfaced in E6 Discussion/Limitations prose (advisory).
